title: Witness and Alibi
premise: August Eriksen is hired to probate the estate of drowned fisherman Halvard Ness, only to discover a will dated three days after his death — signed, witnessed, and legally impossible. The twin letters that follow draw August into the closed world of the Ness family's island village, where everyone has an alibi and someone has been rehearsing theirs for years. As August uncovers that Halvard's death concealed an older crime — the drowning of his business partner decades ago and the stolen inheritance that built the family fortune — the killer begins feeding August evidence, testing whether they will bury the truth or publish it. In the end, August stages a false reading of the will to force a confession before witnesses, and the tide gives up what it took: the partner's ring, lodged in the harbor pilings, proving justice must be done outside the law when the law itself was bought.
about_author: Ulyana Montrose is the pen name of a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing shipwreck estates along the northern coast. Their novels are known for legal precision, salt-bitten atmospheres, and protagonists who believe paperwork can hold a moral line.

chapters.title: The Impossible Date
chapters.summary: POV August. In their cluttered coastal office, August opens the Ness probate file and finds a will dated after the testator's death. The signature is flawless; the witness line names a woman who died in 1998. Emotional beat: professional pride curdling into unease as August realizes someone wanted this document found.

chapters.title: Two Envelopes
chapters.summary: POV August. Twin letters arrive by separate couriers: one confessing to Halvard Ness's murder in careful legalese, the other promising 'the rest of the file' if August reads the will aloud at Friday's gathering. Emotional beat: the thrill of a case they cannot refuse, shadowed by the sense of being cast in someone else's play.

chapters.title: Crossing at Low Water
chapters.summary: POV August. August takes the ferry to Sker Island and meets the Ness heirs: brittle widow Maren, resentful son Torben, and adopted daughter Liv, who watches everything. Each greets the will news with rehearsed calm. Emotional beat: August's outsider status sharpening into belonging-adjacent curiosity.

chapters.title: The House That Halvard Built
chapters.summary: POV August. A tour of the Ness house reveals wealth built on a cannery partnership with one Dag Solheim, who drowned in 1979 — officially an accident. August notices Halvard's study contains no partnership papers at all. Emotional beat: the first crack of doubt about which death the letters confess to.

chapters.title: Alibis Like Tidewater
chapters.summary: POV August. August interviews each heir against the night Halvard drowned. Every account checks out perfectly — too perfectly, each corroborated by another. Emotional beat: mounting frustration as August realizes the alibis were constructed together, like a story told around a fire.

chapters.title: What the Constable Kept
chapters.summary: POV August. The aging island constable, Brandt, shares his private file over aquavit: Halvard's body showed marks he was ordered not to record. He warns August that the last lawyer who asked questions left on the next boat. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance, and the first taste of real danger.

chapters.title: Liv's Version
chapters.summary: POV Liv. On the breakwater, Liv tells August she found her father's old ledger hidden in the boathouse — pages torn out where Solheim's name should appear. She doesn't trust August yet, but wants the truth more than the inheritance. Emotional beat: guarded connection between two people who both live outside the family.

chapters.title: The Second Confession
chapters.summary: POV August. Another letter arrives, confessing again — but describing details of the 1979 drowning that were never public. The handwriting matches the first. Emotional beat: horror dawning as August understands the confessor is confessing to two murders, or one murderer across forty years.

chapters.title: Torben's Debt
chapters.summary: POV August. August discovers Torben has quietly mortgaged his share of the estate twice over; the will, if read, leaves him nearly nothing. He had motive, means, and a boat. But his alibi holds like iron. Emotional beat: the trap of a perfect suspect who cannot be guilty.

chapters.title: Maren's Silence
chapters.summary: POV Maren. The widow remembers the night of Halvard's death: he burned papers in the study fireplace and told her, 'If I go in the water, it's debt coming home.' She has kept silent for thirty years out of love, or fear. Emotional beat: grief revealing itself as complicity.

chapters.title: The Missing Witness
chapters.summary: POV August. August traces the dead witness named on the impossible will — a housekeeper who vanished in 1998, the same year the Solheim file was sealed. Someone with access to old records forged her name. Only four people could have. Emotional beat: the circle tightening, and August inside it.

chapters.title: Storm Warning
chapters.summary: POV August. A threatening note appears pinned inside August's own case file — pages only August has handled. The killer isn't watching from outside; they've been reading along. Emotional beat: violation and vertigo, the investigator becoming the investigated.

chapters.title: The Boathouse Ledger
chapters.summary: POV Liv. Liv and August reconstruct the torn ledger from carbon copies stored in the cannery office: Halvard defrauded Solheim systematically, and Solheim's drowning followed his threat to sue. The fortune, and the will, are built on theft. Emotional beat: shared purpose hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: Brandt's Regret
chapters.summary: POV Brandt. The constable admits he falsified the 1979 report under pressure from Halvard — and that the housekeeper saw him do it. Her disappearance has haunted him since. Emotional beat: confession as penance, an old man handing August the weight he's carried.

chapters.title: Reading the Tide Tables
chapters.summary: POV August. August works out that the killer's letters reference tide conditions only someone present at both drownings would know. The confessor didn't witness the crimes — they committed them, or watched them committed by someone they're protecting. Emotional beat: cold clarity, the trap turning in August's mind.

chapters.title: The Gathering
chapters.summary: POV August. Friday arrives. The heirs assemble in the Ness parlor for the reading. August announces they will not read the will — instead they'll read the reconstructed ledger aloud. The room detonates: denial, accusation, and one face going carefully blank. Emotional beat: controlled chaos, August holding the center.

chapters.title: Blank Page
chapters.summary: POV August. The killer strikes back fast: the ledger copies vanish from August's room, and Brandt is found injured at the boathouse, alive but silenced. August realizes the final letter's promise — 'more' — means a third death is scheduled. Emotional beat: fury and fear fused into urgency.

chapters.title: What the Tide Took
chapters.summary: POV August. At extreme low tide, August searches the harbor pilings where Solheim went down and finds a wedding ring wedged deep in the wood — Solheim's, planted there in 1979 as a trophy or a tether. Whoever kept its twin has been tied to this harbor ever since. Emotional beat: the past surfacing, literal and undeniable.

chapters.title: The Twin Ring
chapters.summary: POV August. August confronts the truth: Maren was Solheim's lover before marrying Halvard; she witnessed both drownings and wrote the confessions to force the family's reckoning without naming herself. But the killings weren't hers — Torben learned of the letters and acted to protect his inheritance. Emotional beat: pity and horror entwined.

chapters.title: The False Reading
chapters.summary: POV August. August stages a second reading, announcing the will leaves everything to the memory of Dag Solheim — and that the original 1979 fraud file goes to the mainland police at dawn unless the killer speaks now. Torben breaks, lunging for the file, confessing before the assembled family and Brandt's recorder. Emotional beat: cathartic collapse, justice seizing its moment.

chapters.title: Belonging
chapters.summary: POV Liv. In the aftermath, Torben is taken to the mainland; Maren chooses to stay and face the island's judgment rather than flee. Liv offers August a permanent place as the estate's counsel — the outsider invited in. Emotional beat: bittersweet belonging earned through truth rather than blood.

chapters.title: Closing the File
chapters.summary: POV August. Back in their office, August writes the closing letter: the case is closed, though not by the law alone. They keep Solheim's ring on their desk, a paperweight for every future will they draft. Emotional beat: quiet resolution — some inheritances are debts, and August has learned to collect them.
